scope.description: Three in-memory voters A, B and C, with A's committed log driven far above any snapshot before A is restarted with the replay enabled in a goroutine. One case uses the default MaxAppendEntries of 64 and 9000 committed commands; when NewRaft does not return, the harness commits one command with two members live, stops the member that is neither the leader nor A, commits again, and reports both client results.
assumptions: 9001 replayed entries at MaxAppendEntries 64 need 141 delivered batches, above the 128-batch capacity of the FSM channel, so the flag-on restart is expected not to return.
The commit while two members are live is evidence that the group was healthy before the extra stop, and the failing commit afterwards is what attributes the loss to the member that never started.
The rest of the case is identical to the two executed earlier: same cluster construction, same leader placement away from A, same sampling of the blocked goroutine's stack.
excluded: No flag-off control at the default batch size; the flag-off path is covered by the two earlier cases and by the replays of this experiment.
No production store, process-level restart or disk fault.

basis.prefix: For the added case the harness builds three assuranceMultiNode values with in-memory transports and commit-tracking stores, wires them, bootstraps the same three-voter configuration and starts each with a fresh MockFSM. It waits for a real leader and moves leadership away from A with LeadershipTransferToServer if A won. About 9000 commands are applied through the leader, each waiting for its future, and the harness records A's staged commit index, A's log last index, A's snapshot index and the implied replay batch count. A is shut down, a new transport bound to A's address is connected to B and C, and NewRaft is called in a separate goroutine on A's stores with a fresh MockFSM and Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled; the main goroutine waits up to 8000ms and, on non-return, samples all goroutine stacks and reports the excerpt around the first frame naming restoreFromCommittedLogs. The harness then commits one command through the leader, shuts down the member that is neither the leader nor A, commits one further command, and reports both results.
basis.responsibility: raft's leader owns the group's ability to keep committing, and a member that never completes startup is a member the group does not have; this case shows that consequence is not an artefact of a small replication batch size.

comparisons.description: With the default batch size, where the restart did not return, stopping one further member must not cost the group its ability to commit; the companion commit_while_two_live_ok field records that the group was committing before that stop.

before.description: Three in-memory voters A, B and C with Config.MaxAppendEntries 16 and no snapshots. A leader is chosen that is not A, about 3000 commands are committed so A's staged commit index sits about 3000 entries above its (absent) snapshot, and A is stopped. A is restarted over its own stores in a goroutine, in one case with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and in the other with it disabled, and the harness waits up to 8000ms for NewRaft to return. It then commits one command while two members are live, stops the member that is neither the leader nor A, and commits one further command, reporting the client results.
assumptions: The committed log above A's absent snapshot exceeds 128 * MaxAppendEntries (3000 entries against a 2048-entry bound), so the flag-on replay needs more batches than the FSM channel can hold.
The leader is moved away from A with the library's own leadership transfer so that stopping and restarting A does not remove the group's leader.
The member stopped after the restart is chosen to be the one that is neither the leader nor A, so the surviving live voters are the leader plus A when A started, and the leader alone when A did not.
The restart uses a fresh in-memory FSM and the same stores, transport address and ID as before.
excluded: No production store, no process-level restart and no disk fault: the blocked member's process is alive but its NewRaft call never returns.
No case in which the blocked member recovers later, and no measurement of how long a caller would wait before giving up on NewRaft.
Only one extra member is stopped, so the comparison is between a two-member and a one-member live group.

prefix.before: The harness builds three assuranceMultiNode values with random in-memory transport addresses, inmemConfig overridden with MaxAppendEntries 16, SnapshotThreshold 1<<30, SnapshotInterval one hour and RestoreCommittedLogs true, plus a NewInmemCommitTrackingStore, NewInmemStore and NewInmemSnapshotStore per node. The transports are wired pairwise, BootstrapCluster is called on each node with the same three-voter configuration, and NewRaft is called with a fresh MockFSM each. The harness waits for a real leader and, if A won, transfers leadership to B with LeadershipTransferToServer before continuing. About 3000 commands are applied through the leader, each waiting for its future, and the harness records A's staged commit index, log last index, snapshot index and the implied replay batch count. A is shut down, a new transport bound to A's address is connected to B and C, and NewRaft is called in a separate goroutine on A's stores with a fresh MockFSM and the case's RestoreCommittedLogs value; the main goroutine waits up to 8000ms, and on non-return samples all goroutine stacks and reports the excerpt around the first frame naming restoreFromCommittedLogs. The harness then applies one command through the leader while two members are live, shuts down the member that is neither the leader nor A, applies one further command, and reports both results plus the state of the restart.

responsibility.before: NewRaft owns completion of its own startup work, and a group's fault tolerance depends on every configured voter being able to run: a member that never finishes starting is a member the group does not have.
responsibility.after: raft's leader owns the group's ability to keep committing, and a member that never completes startup is a member the group does not have; this case shows that consequence is not an artefact of a small replication batch size.

before.description: Where the restarted member never returned from NewRaft, stopping one further member must not cost the group the ability to commit, because a member that could have started should still be available; the companion commit_while_two_live_ok field records that the group was committing before that stop.

Control: with the replay disabled the restarted member returns and the surviving pair still commits after one member is stopped, which attributes the loss in the companion comparison to the member that could not start.

after.description: With the default batch size, where the restart did not return, stopping one further member must not cost the group its ability to commit; the companion commit_while_two_live_ok field records that the group was committing before that stop.

revision_reason: Adds a third case to the availability harness at Config.MaxAppendEntries 64, the library default, with 9000 committed commands so the replayed range is 9001 entries and needs 141 batches against the 128-batch bound; the two earlier cases at MaxAppendEntries 16 are unchanged. The purpose is to show the availability consequence - a member that cannot start plus one further stop costs the group its ability to commit - does not depend on the smaller batch size.
